author: NotPineapple203
body:
Hey guys, so this is a work in progress, and I just want your opinion on it. I'm guessing its meant to be around a 15-20 per team match. Inside the hourglass in the middle island there are two diamond blocks and in the side islands with the chests there are 2 golden apples and one diamond sword. There are 1024 blocks of iron and two monuments per side. I have only made one side so I wouldn't have to do as much work before i asked for opinions. Please give me your opinion and any advice that you have.
     Thank you,
           pineapple203

IMAGES:
http://imgur.com/a/i6xot

title: Hourglass [DTM]  Advice/Opinion?

replies.author: Arcaous
replies.body: I'm no grade A expert on maps, but from what I've seen over the years this seems to a pretty solid work so far. Any idea how many monuments or wool you plan on putting in?
replies.body_tagged: I'm no grade A expert on maps, but from what I've seen over the years this seems to a pretty solid work so far. Any idea how many monuments or wool you plan on putting in?

replies.author: Crimson_Aught
replies.body:
This map looks like old ones for now.
Maybe change design, make monument islands bigger and farther from each other. Also you can build 3 monuments instead of 2.
replies.body_tagged:

replies.author: NotPineapple203
replies.body:
That almost what i was going for. I've been on the server for a very long time and I still remember the day rendezvous II came out. I liked how simplistic they were and i notice now a days many maps seem to be very detailed and computer intensive, which in my opinion is meaningless. We play the game not because its pretty we play it because it's fun.

I also feel like if i fit in 3 monuments into the back it would be difficult to space them out. I will take the advice of making them bigger though. 
Thank You for your feedback

replies.author: Arcaous
replies.body: This did remind me of the fun style used in the Rendezvous maps and others like it. Could always consider elongating or expanding some sections of the map, but don't want to get too caught up in sentiment  or you might end up making a clone map. Curious to see what your final product is though

replies.body:
